story.title: Datta’s siddhi display dismisses incessant attendants
story.completeness_basis: Entire bounded cited Sanskrit arc read; significant named actors, relationships, boons/powers, dialogue and transition checks by author. Independent root review separate.

event.details: Datta, Viṣṇu kalāṃśa, attains successive Brahman/yoga states such as inert/mad/piśāca/child-joy states. People of all varṇas/āśramas serve him, leaving no rest; distressed he submerges by yoga while they wait at shore. By siddhi he manifests Mokṣalakṣmī, rises holding her at left and wine-pot in right, drinks/enjoys with her. They judge him fallen and abandon him, allowing peaceful yoga. This is a narrated withdrawal stratagem; Mokṣalakṣmī is not silently identified with Viṣṇu’s ordinary spouse.
